subject: QBR playbook: Acme engagement — customer wellness, renewal risk register & exec asks
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: QBR playbook: Acme engagement — customer wellness, renewal risk register & exec asks

Team — putting together a tight playbook for next week's QBR with Acme (renewal in 10 weeks). High-level ask: please review the attached playbook and the renewal risk register and confirm owners for the top three mitigation items by EOD Wednesday. Key context below and explicit exec asks at the bottom.

Quick read points:
- Account size: ~ $1.4M annual run-rate (multi-product). Renewal window: early Apr 2027.
- Current usage: steady token consumption but a 12% drop in query volume in last 30 days (marketing A/B ended).
- Recent incident: two 30-45s latency spikes for batch ingestion on 2027-01-21 (postmortem attached in Drive link).

Attached artifacts: acme-qbr-playbook-v1.pdf; acme-renewal-risk-register.csv; mutual-action-plan-draft.docx. Also linking the HubSpot deal and the MAP DocuSign template.

Primary goals for the QBR:
1) Reassure execs on stability and roadmap for low-latency serving for their burst windows.
2) Lock in a firm renewal timeline and procurement checklist (we need PO by 2027-03-25 to hit renewal).
3) Agree on a pilot for Dedicated capacity for peak marketing events (cost/throughput trade-offs).

Exec attention items (please mark who will lead each):
A) Stability narrative and SLO adjustments (owner: ?) — need a short one-pager for the CTO.
B) Commercial concession ask — they requested a 10% anchor credit for early renewal; finance needs scenario modeling.
C) Procurement blocker — Acme procurement requires SOC2 evidence and an updated DPA; Legal needs to confirm turnaround.

Marissa: can you take A and own the SLO one-pager? Karthik: can you take B and run a quick concession impact with Finance? I will coordinate Legal for C and draft the exec slide.

Please reply with owners/ETA. I want a dry run on Friday morning (30m) so we can rehearse the ask and fallback positions.

Thanks —
Ava Chen
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR playbook: Acme engagement — customer wellness, renewal risk register & exec asks

Thanks Ava — I skimmed the playbook and the risk register. I'll own A (SLO narrative). Plan:
- Draft a one-pager that: 1) summarizes the incident root cause, 2) lists mitigations we've implemented, and 3) proposes a temporary SLO window for the next 90 days with measurable rollback triggers.
- ETA: first draft Wed 12:00pm PT.

Two quick notes from my side:
1) On the incident — the latency spikes correlated with an unexpected Kafka rebalance during a geo-shift; ops already put a conservative autoscale increase in place for their ingest pool. I'll include the postmortem bullet summary.
2) For the exec narrative, we should call out the Dedicated pilot as an optional path but not a hard ask on day one; frame it as "insurance for high-volume campaigns."

I'll add the one-pager to the Drive folder and paste here when ready. Friday dry run works — prefer 8:30am PT.

Marissa
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

I'll take B (commercial concession modeling). Quick read of the numbers: a 10% anchor credit on a $1.4M ARR deal is roughly $140k annual equivalent; with a 12-month renewal that reduces first-year revenue materially. I'll run two scenarios: 1) 10% upfront credit + 12-month term extension, 2) a smaller 5% credit + an adoption milestone-based rebate.

ETA: I'll have scenario slides and a recommended concession path by Thu 10:30am PT so Finance has time to weigh in before the Friday dry run. Also will add an ask to collect their procurement timeline (Procurement email in CC on our outreach) so Legal can prioritize the DPA.

Karthik

Redwood Inference

Ava — thanks for the heads up and for the detailed materials. Quick notes from our side:
- Procurement: tentative PO timeline is mid-March but we are trying to accelerate to the first week of March; I will confirm by Friday.
- The exec asks are reasonable. Our CTO wants the stability one-pager and a clear SLA step-down plan before the QBR — happy for Marissa to send that directly to him.
- On the commercial ask: our Finance lead prefers milestone-linked concessions (e.g., 50% of the credit releases after migration completion). We can discuss in the QBR.

I'll review the playbook this evening and get Procurement added to the MAP DocuSign request if we move forward.

Best,
Alex Jordan
Director of Platform Engineering
Acme Corp
